record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.context_brief: ISS versus iISS for L∞ inputs
record.original_question: For linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators and input space L∞(R+, U), does input-to-state stability imply integral input-to-state stability? More specifically, after knowing that iISS implies ISS in this setting, determine whether the reverse implication ISS ⇒ iISS also holds for L∞ inputs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.22. In view of Proposition 3.20 we know that for U := L∞(R+, U), integral ISS implies ISS. At the same time, the question whether ISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) implies iISS w.r.t. L∞(R+, U) is a challenging open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ and $U$ be Banach spaces, and consider a linear control system
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), \qquad x(0) = x_0 \in X, \qquad t \geq 0,$$
where $A : D(A) \subset X \to X$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$ and $B \in \mathcal{L}(U, X_{-1})$ is a (possibly) unbounded admissible control operator, with $X_{-1}$ the usual extrapolation space associated with $A$. For an admissible input space $\mathcal{U} = L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$, the mild solution is
$$x(t; x_0, u) = T(t) x_0 + \int_0^t T_{-1}(t-s) B u(s)\, ds \in X.$$

Definitions.
1. The system is input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every $u \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$,
$$\|x(t; x_0, u)\|_X \leq \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{L^\infty(0,t;U)}), \qquad t \ge 0.$$
2. The system is integral input-to-state stable (iISS) with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\theta, \mu \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every $u \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$,
$$\|x(t; x_0, u)\|_X \leq \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \theta\!\left(\int_0^t \mu(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds\right), \qquad t \ge 0.$$

It is known that, in this setting, iISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ implies ISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$.

Question. For linear infinite-dimensional systems of the above form with possibly unbounded admissible control operator $B$, does ISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ imply iISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on ISS for infinite-dimensional linear systems (including works on L^p–L^q ISS and Orlicz-space characterizations through 2025) treats the question of whether ISS w.r.t. L^∞ implies iISS w.r.t. L^∞ for unbounded admissible control operators as still open in general. Equivalence has been established only in special classes (e.g., parabolic diagonal systems), but no general resolution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability in integral norms for linear infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Develops L^p–L^q ISS theory and admissibility characterizations but does not establish a general equivalence between classical ISS and iISS for L^∞ inputs with unbounded control operators.
status_evidence.claim: The general implication ISS ⇒ iISS for L^∞ inputs with unbounded B is not resolved in this 2025 work.

status_evidence.title: Infinite-Dimensional Input-to-State Stability and Orlicz Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: For parabolic diagonal systems, ISS and iISS coincide even for L^∞ inputs; the general unbounded case is not settled.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence is known only in special structured cases.
